sentences.text:
The PI Govindraj nagar Police station has filed chargesheet against accused for the offences punishable u/s.498A, 504, 506 r/w 34 of IPC and u/s. 3 & 4 of DP Act.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the prosecution are that on 28.11.2022 marriage of CW1 was solemnized with the accused at Veeranjeneya Temple, Saraswathi Nagar,
Bangalore and at the time of marriage, 16 gms of golden chain , 5gms of golden ring and jewels were given to Cw 1 and the marriage was performed by spending approximately Rs.5 lakhs.
After the marriage, CW 1 was residing with the accused and his parents at their house situated at Vidyanagar, near Vasavi School, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagar  3 CC.No.9018/23 District.
Cw 1 was working in a private company and she used to travel from Bangalore to Magadi and sometime she used to go home at 10.00p.m.
Since Cw 1 used to go home very late, the accused asked Cw 1 to quite the job, but, Cw 1 did not agree.

Since Cw 1 did not agree to quit the job, the accused asked to pick up quarrel for silly reasons and subject Cw 1 to cruelty mentally and physically and tortured Cw 1 for additional dowry and also abused Cw 1 in filthy wordings and threatened her with dire consequence of life and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.498A, 504, 506 R/W.34 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
 3.
On the basis of the complaint of the CW 1, this crime has been registered by Govindraj Nagar Police Station against accused No.1 to 7.

After investigation, Investigating officer filed the charge sheet against accused No.1 for the offences punishable u/s. 498A, 504, 506 R/W.34 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of D.P.Act and dropped the case against accusedNo. 2 to 7 .
The cognizance for the said offences are taken .
4. Since the accused No.1 was on anticipatory bail, on issuance of summons he appeared through counsel and filed bail application and enlarged on bail.

The copies of the  4 CC.No.9018/23 prosecution papers have furnished to the accused No.1 as Govindarajanagar Police Station vs Naveen Kumar S N on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119289101/

sentences.text: Point No.1 to 4:
Since all these points are interlinked with each other, I have taken them together for common discussion in order to avoid the repetition.

According to the prosecution,
accused No.1 has committed the offences u/s.498A, 504,
506 R/W.34 OF IPC and Sec.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
In order to prove the guilt of the accused , the prosecution has examined the complainant as PW.1.
The PW 1 has deposed that she and accused got married on 28.10.2022 at Veeranjeneya Swamy temple Saraswathi Nagar .
After marriage, she has been residing with the accused.
Accused has not assaulted and abused her and he has not caused any dowry  7 CC.No.9018/23 harassement.
About 1 year ago back, when she went to police station, they have took the signature on two documents which are the complaint and mahazar and they have marked as Ex.P.1 & 2.

She has deposed that she does not know what Govindarajanagar Police Station vs Naveen Kumar S N on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119289101/
4 has written in Ex.P.1 & 2.

sentences.text: Thus she has totally turned hostile to the case of the prosecution.
10. At request of learned senior APP this witness has been treated as hostile witness and permission was accorded to cross examine her.
In the cross examination the learned Sr.APP suggested the case of the prosecution and same has been denied by the witness.
On the basis of the above evidence of PW.1 the court cannot come to conclusion that the accused No.1 has not committed the offence as alleged by the prosecution.
If really there was any incident, definitely the PW.1 should have given evidence on par with the avernments made in the complaint.
Here the PW.1 turned hostile, in the cross examination she has categorically admitted that, she and accused have compromised the matter.
That is the reason why PW.1 has not given any evidence supporting the case of the prosecution.

In a criminal justice system, if a tiny doubt arises in the mind of the court,
benefit of doubt shall be extended to the accused persons.

In this case, not only tiny doubt but the strong doubt arise in the mind of the court, because the victim herself has not  8 CC.No.9018/
supported the case of the prosecution.

Hence, 
prosecution has utterly failed to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, in my opinion it is a fit case to extend benefit of doubt to the accused .
Accordingly point Nos 1 to 4 are answered in the Negative.
11. POINT NO.5 :

For the aforesaid reason and discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. Accused No.1 is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable U/s. 498A, 504, 506, r/w34 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of D.P.Act .
The bail bond executed by the accused No.1 stands cancelled.

However, Accused No.1 shall execute personal bond of Rs.50,000/-
by undertaking to appear before the Honble appellate Court, if any appeal is filed.

It is not a fit case to award victim compensation as provided U/s.357(1) of Cr.P.C., (Dictated to the stenographer,
script transcribed by her and then corrected directly on computer and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 16 th day of April 2024).
(B.C.CHANDRASHEKAR) XXIV A.C.M.M., BENGALURU.
ANNEXURE
